---
title: "Input representation and the detectability floor"
output:
  pdf_document: {fig_width: 11, fig_height: 8.5}
  html_document: {fig_width: 11, fig_height: 8.5}
---

<!--
WHAT THIS FIGURE IS FOR

Every gate in v7.3 is computed on treated (X) libraries, so a virus with no oligos in the pool and a
virus with oligos but no xrRNA give the identical result: zero passing sites. This figure separates
them, using the control (R) libraries, which measure representation alone.

It also draws the derivation of the stall-read floor rather than asserting a number, because the
number is not transferable between libraries and the procedure is.

ONE NOTEBOOK, TWO FIGURES. Set LIB below and knit twice. The panels are identical for the two
libraries, and two separate files would drift apart; the only differences are paths, the replicate
gate, and the number of conditions, all handled by the switch.

INPUTS come from scripts/detectability_floor.py:
  representation/input_representation.tsv   per accession: tiles, R_med, R_min, R_total, band
  representation/detectability_floor.txt    the report; the floor is parsed out of it, not retyped
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, dev = "cairo_pdf")
library(tidyverse); library(scales); library(patchwork)
```

```{r config}
# ---- THE ONLY THING TO CHANGE BETWEEN THE TWO KNITS -------------------------------------
LIB <- "flaviLib"          # "flaviLib" or "viromelib"

CFG <- list(
  flaviLib = list(
    base      = "~/Desktop/viromelib/flaviLib/figures/representation",
    rep_tsv   = "flaviLib_input_representation.tsv",
    floor_txt = "flaviLib_detectability_floor.txt",
    taxonomy  = "virus_taxonomy_flaviLib_261021.csv",
    gate      = "2 of 4 replicates",
    tiling    = "196 nt tiles, 20 nt step",
    # Accessions worth naming on the depth panel. HCV is here BECAUSE it is the failure case:
    # it is in the library and was never assayable, which is the whole point of the figure.
    label = tribble(
      ~accession,     ~nm,
      "NC_024077.1",  "SbCNV-5",
      "NC_006551.1",  "Usutu",
      "NC_015843.2",  "Tembusu",
      "NC_009942.1",  "West Nile",
      "NC_012532.1",  "Zika",
      "NC_004102.1",  "HCV (H77)",
      "NC_009827.1",  "HCV"
    )
  ),
  viromelib = list(
    base      = "~/Desktop/viromelib/figures/representation",
    rep_tsv   = "viromelib_input_representation.tsv",
    floor_txt = "viromelib_detectability_floor.txt",
    taxonomy  = "virus_taxonomy_viromelib_261019.csv",
    gate      = "2 of 3 replicates",
    tiling    = "tiles at 80 nt step",
    label     = tibble(accession = character(), nm = character())
  )
)[[LIB]]

# Directory convention -- the SAME one the already-run notebooks use, so nothing here is a new
# scheme to remember:
#   <figure>/inputs/                  FLAT. The run is in the FILENAME, not a subdirectory, so it
#                                     travels with the file if it is ever copied or attached.
#   <figure>/plots/<date>_<strategy>/ outputs, so a re-run never overwrites an older figure.
STRATEGY <- paste0("20261026_floor_besttile_", LIB)
INDIR    <- file.path(path.expand(CFG$base), "inputs")
OUTDIR   <- file.path(path.expand(CFG$base), "plots", STRATEGY)
dir.create(OUTDIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Bands are an ordered factor everywhere, so colour and legend order never depend on which
# bands happen to be populated in a given library.
BAND_LEVELS <- c("not_assayed", "marginal", "assayed")
BAND_LABS <- c(not_assayed = "not assayed (absence uninformative)",
               marginal    = "marginal (absence weak evidence)",
               assayed     = "assayed (absence is a real negative)")
BAND_COLS <- c(not_assayed = "#b2182b", marginal = "#e8a33d", assayed = "#4393c3")
```

```{r load}
rep_path <- file.path(INDIR, CFG$rep_tsv)
stopifnot("input_representation.tsv not found — copy it down from the cluster" =
            file.exists(rep_path))
d <- read_tsv(rep_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename(accession = 1) |>
  mutate(band = factor(as.character(band), levels = BAND_LEVELS))

# Parse the floor out of the report rather than retyping it. A number typed into a notebook
# drifts from the number the script derived; this cannot.
floor_path <- file.path(INDIR, CFG$floor_txt)
stopifnot("detectability_floor.txt not found" = file.exists(floor_path))
ftxt <- read_lines(floor_path)
num <- function(pat) {
  ln <- str_subset(ftxt, pat)
  stopifnot("could not parse the floor report — has its format changed?" = length(ln) >= 1)
  parse_number(str_extract(ln[1], "[0-9][0-9,\\.]*"))
}
FLOOR    <- num("^FLOOR")
MARGINAL <- num("^MARGINAL top")
LIB_MED  <- num("library median control reads/tile")
RHO      <- as.numeric(str_extract(str_subset(ftxt, "Spearman")[1], "[-+][0-9.]+"))

# Depth at called sites, the derivation itself. Pulled from the report table so the panel shows
# exactly the numbers the floor was set from.
called <- ftxt |>
  (\(x) x[seq(which(str_detect(x, "^control depth AT SITES THAT PASSED"))[1] + 2, length(x))])() |>
  head(6) |>
  str_match("^\\s+(\\S+)\\s+([0-9,]+)\\s+([0-9,]+)\\s+([0-9,]+)\\s+([0-9,]+)\\s+([0-9,]+)") |>
  as_tibble(.name_repair = "minimal") |>
  setNames(c("raw", "cond", "n_sites", "unmatched", "min_depth", "p1", "median_depth")) |>
  filter(!is.na(cond)) |>
  mutate(across(c(n_sites, unmatched, min_depth, p1, median_depth), parse_number))

tax <- {
  p <- file.path(INDIR, CFG$taxonomy)
  if (file.exists(p)) read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE) else tibble()
}
if (nrow(tax)) {
  acc_col <- intersect(c("accession", "plain_accession"), names(tax))[1]
  d <- d |> left_join(tax |> select(accession = all_of(acc_col), any_of(c("family", "genus"))) |>
                        distinct(accession, .keep_all = TRUE), by = "accession")
}
lab <- CFG$label |> inner_join(d, by = "accession")
```

```{r panelA, fig.height=4}
# PANEL A — the depth distribution, with the floor drawn on it.
# log10 x: the range spans six orders of magnitude, so a linear axis would collapse the entire
# unassayable tail into the first pixel, which is precisely the part being argued about.
pA <- ggplot(d, aes(R_med + 1)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = FLOOR, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = BAND_COLS[["not_assayed"]], alpha = 0.10) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = FLOOR, xmax = MARGINAL, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = BAND_COLS[["marginal"]], alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = band), bins = 55, colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(FLOOR, MARGINAL), linetype = c("solid", "dashed"), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = LIB_MED, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = BAND_COLS, labels = BAND_LABS, drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey70") +
  labs(x = "median control (R) reads per tile", y = "accessions", fill = NULL,
       title = "A  Input representation per accession",
       subtitle = sprintf(
         "solid: floor %s reads/tile  |  dashed: marginal top %s  |  dotted: library median %s",
         comma(FLOOR), comma(MARGINAL), comma(LIB_MED))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5))

if (nrow(lab)) {
  pA <- pA + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = lab, aes(x = R_med + 1, y = 0, label = nm),
    size = 2.5, direction = "y", nudge_y = 6, segment.size = 0.2,
    min.segment.length = 0, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 1)
}
pA
```

```{r panelB, fig.height=4}
# PANEL B — the derivation, drawn. The minimum depth at a site that actually passed IS the floor;
# showing it next to the full distribution is the argument for the number.
pB <- ggplot(called, aes(cond)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = min_depth, ymax = median_depth), linewidth = 0.5, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(y = median_depth), size = 2.4, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(aes(y = p1), size = 2.0, shape = 21, fill = BAND_COLS[["marginal"]]) +
  geom_point(aes(y = min_depth), size = 2.6, shape = 23, fill = BAND_COLS[["not_assayed"]]) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = FLOOR, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(y = min_depth, label = comma(min_depth)), hjust = -0.35, size = 2.6) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "control (R) reads per tile",
       title = "B  How the floor was determined",
       subtitle = paste0("diamond = MINIMUM depth at a site passing ", CFG$gate,
                         "; circle = 1st percentile; dot = median.\n",
                         "No site was ever called below the diamond, so absence below it ",
                         "carries no information.")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5))
pB
```

```{r panelC, fig.height=4}
# PANEL C — is sensitivity uniform across feature length?
# Reads PER TILE should not depend on how many tiles an accession contributes if the oligo pool
# were equimolar. A gradient means sensitivity is systematically lower for short features, which
# weakens every "family X has no xrRNA" claim for short-UTR families.
pC <- ggplot(d, aes(tiles, R_med + 1)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = band), alpha = 0.55, size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = FLOOR, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = BAND_COLS, drop = FALSE, guide = "none", na.value = "grey70") +
  labs(x = "tiles contributed by the accession (log)", y = "median control reads per tile (log)",
       title = "C  Is sensitivity uniform across feature length?",
       subtitle = sprintf(
         "Spearman %+.3f. A flat cloud would mean uniform sensitivity; a slope means short\nfeatures were assayed less deeply, so absence is weaker evidence for them.", RHO)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5))
pC
```

```{r panelD, fig.height=4.2}
# PANEL D — which taxa fall in which band. Only drawn if taxonomy joined; a figure that silently
# omits a panel is worse than one that says why.
if ("family" %in% names(d) && sum(!is.na(d$family)) > 0) {
  fam <- d |> filter(!is.na(family)) |>
    count(family, band, .drop = FALSE) |>
    group_by(family) |> mutate(tot = sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
    filter(tot >= 3) |>
    mutate(family = fct_reorder(family, tot))
  pD <- ggplot(fam, aes(n, family, fill = band)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.72) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = BAND_COLS, labels = BAND_LABS, drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey70") +
    labs(x = "accessions", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "D  Representation by family",
         subtitle = "families with >= 3 accessions") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical",
          legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5))
} else {
  pD <- ggplot() + theme_void() +
    annotate("text", 0, 0, size = 3,
             label = "Panel D omitted: no taxonomy file found.\nCopy the taxonomy CSV into inputs/.")
}
pD
```

```{r assemble}
fig <- (pA | pB) / (pC | pD) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = sprintf("Input representation and the detectability floor \u2014 %s", LIB),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      paste("%s | %s | gate %s | library median %s control reads/tile.",
            "Depth measured in CONTROL (R) libraries only: treated depth confounds representation",
            "with stalling, so a fully degraded virus and an absent virus are indistinguishable there."),
      LIB, CFG$tiling, CFG$gate, comma(LIB_MED)),
    theme = theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)))

ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, sprintf("representation_floor_%s.pdf", LIB)),
       fig, width = 13, height = 10, device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, sprintf("representation_floor_%s.png", LIB)),
       fig, width = 13, height = 10, dpi = 300)
fig
```

```{r tables}
# Numbers for the legend and for RZ, written out rather than read off the plot.
summ <- d |> count(band, .drop = FALSE) |> mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))
write_csv(summ, file.path(OUTDIR, sprintf("band_counts_%s.csv", LIB)))
write_csv(d |> filter(band != "assayed") |> arrange(R_med),
          file.path(OUTDIR, sprintf("accessions_below_assayed_%s.csv", LIB)))
knitr::kable(summ, digits = 1, caption = sprintf("%s: accessions by band", LIB))
```
